title: Geo-informed vendor scoring & latency arbitrage playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce an operational playbook and scoring rubric that the PM and GTM teams can use to prioritize model vendors and fallback choices by geography (initial focus: APAC, EU, NA). Motivation: regional latency and model availability are creating fragmented customer experiences; we need a repeatable research + decision process that ties model capabilities, pricing, and operational cost to customer SLAs and go-to-market commitments. This ticket scopes the research plan, the data signals to collect, the scoring model, and the minimum deliverables for an MVP playbook.

Scope:
- Define geographic buckets (region, city clusters, edge nodes) and latency bands that matter to customer cohorts.
- Inventory candidate model vendors and variants for each region (hosted and on-prem compatible).
- Collect signals: measured 95p token latency from sample workloads, regional model availability, quantization/variant latency delta, per-token cost, SDK integration complexity, legal/compliance footnotes (data residency), and procurement friction.
- Build a vendor-region scoring rubric mapping to recommended routing policies (primary, warm-fallback, cold-fallback), cost thresholds, and SLA guardrails.
- Deliverables: one-page playbook, scoring spreadsheet, sample routing-policy YAMLs, and a short internal README for sales/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric implemented in a shared spreadsheet with region/vendor rows and explainable metric columns
At least 6 candidate vendors evaluated across 3 regions with measured latency traces attached
Routing policy templates (primary/warm/cold fallback) documented for two customer archetypes: low-latency tier and cost-optimized tier
Playbook one-pager and a README are reviewed and approved by runtime and solutions engineering
Handover session scheduled with GTM and documentation link shared in Confluence
notes: We're focusing on practical, measurable signals rather than speculative model capability claims. Prior work (see PM-4217) covers model buckets; this ticket operationalizes selection and routing by geography.
